conclusion.strongest_supported_statement: A real policy-amplification cycle is visible at the state-transition level: a premature-finalization incident is converted into activity-state continuation lessons; a broader active-tail form becomes global; the rule is neither sufficient to prevent stopping nor necessary for overprocessing; later policy revisions explicitly classify active-tail and then adjacent scope-expansion clauses as regressions and guard against their return.

architecture_implication.rule: Do not promote a task-local incident lesson directly into a machine-wide completion predicate. A proposed global lesson should first survive a paired same-model replay that tests both the original false-negative and the opposite false-positive, name its scope/trigger explicitly, and have a rollback or demotion criterion.
architecture_implication.why: The observed history shows local corrections can become broader activity predicates, while the same predicates can fail to solve the original problem and coexist with opposite-direction scope errors.
